paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: Random (light color) and random (darker color) performance comparison with different perturbation setups and the unperturbed trained model variants (orange bars). Left-to-right: Blue: Accuracy of the embedding and first layers' probes; Green: Random models with pre-trained embedding layer: no perturbation, , , , ; Red: Random models where the embedding layer is random as well: no perturbation, , , , ; Orange: Unperturbed trained models.
model_annotation: The chart illustrates classification accuracy across a series of model/probe configurations and perturbation setups, shown as paired bars in two shades for each category, with the final category representing unperturbed trained models in orange. The horizontal axis contains the categorical conditions, ordered left-to-right as: “embedding,” “1st layer,” “random layers,” “random layers +B2,” “random layers +L2,” “random layers +R2,” “random layers +permute,” “random,” “random +B2,” “random +L2,” “random +R2,” “random +permute,” and “unperturbed,” with labels rotated diagonally. The vertical axis is labeled “Accuracy” and uses a linear scale ranging from 70 to 95, with evenly spaced tick marks every 5 units (70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95). Each category shows two adjacent bars: a lighter-colored bar and a darker-colored bar in the same hue family; the first two categories use light/dark blue, the next five use light/dark green, the following five use light pink/dark red, and the final “unperturbed” category uses light/dark orange. Approximate bar heights are: “embedding” ~80 (light blue) and ~82.2 (dark blue); “1st layer” ~81.8 (light blue) and ~82.2 (dark blue); “random layers” ~79.7 (light green) and ~81.9 (dark green); “random layers +B2” ~79.6 and ~81.5; “random layers +L2” ~79.5 and ~81.6; “random layers +R2” ~79.4 and ~81.7; “random layers +permute” ~79.3 and ~81.4; “random” ~71.8 (light pink) and ~73.5 (dark red); “random +B2” ~72.0 and ~73.6; “random +L2” ~71.9 and ~73.4; “random +R2” ~71.6 and ~73.4; “random +permute” ~71.7 and ~73.1; and “unperturbed” ~90.5 (light orange) and ~91.8–92.0 (dark orange). The bars are not displayed as sorted by magnitude; there are no visible annotations, outlines, or callouts highlighting particular bars beyond the consistent use of color families and light/dark shading to indicate the two paired measurements per category.
